title: Modular Microtranche Playbook: surge staffing, skill-swap protocol, and rolling scope cut rules
creator: Nora Patel
description: Create a practical, repeatable playbook for splitting cycle capacity into small, modular microtranches that can be allocated, reallocated, or deferred with minimal coordination friction. The playbook covers three coordinated levers: (1) surge staffing lanes (temporary reassignments and floating contractors), (2) a skill-swap protocol to match critical skills to urgent slices without overloading squads, and (3) rolling scope-cut rules that let PMs and Eng leads safely trim work while preserving OKR outcomes. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle decision latency, lower cost of rebalancing, and make scope cuts predictable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: A written playbook document published to Confluence with step-by-step surge activation and deactivation flow
Staffing runbook templates (swap request email, on-call surge checklist, handoff checklist) added to repo and Drive
Two simulated microtranche rebalances executed in practice (dry-run) with time-to-deploy metrics recorded
OKR mapping table that shows for each initiative which metrics are protected by mandatory lanes and which are optional
Dashboard widgets in Console for 'surge utilization', 'microtranche velocity', and 'rebalancing latency' linked from the playbook
decisions: Microtranche size standardized at 1-3 engineer-weeks of effort (configurable per discipline), decided to minimize context-switch churn
Surge pool will be a blended pool: 40% reassignable full-time engineers, 40% cross-functional float, 20% contractors/contract-to-hire
Skill-swap requests require triage by the cycle steward; auto-approval allowed for non-blocking swaps under 24 hours
Scope-cut rules: mandatory gating on any feature with >5% projected impact to an OKR metric; otherwise PM-driven discretionary trim
Fallback escalation: if surge pool exhausted, fall back to A/B defer policy (defer >50% of low-impact items) and notify exec sponsor
